reading.body:
Jamie Raskin's AI record in this data is mostly money: 12 of 18 events are political committee contributions from Google, Amazon, Intel, Microsoft, and Oracle, totaling $21,500 between March 2025 and May 2026.

The contributions are small and repeated rather than large and singular. Google gives four times, Amazon three, Intel twice, Microsoft twice, Oracle once. That pattern is consistent with routine PAC giving to a member of Congress, not with a single decisive transfer of influence. The committee names are the AI-relevant fact: these are the same firms building and operating data centers, and their PACs are the mechanism by which they maintain contact with members who sit on the committees that touch them.

The legislative side is thinner. Four recorded votes appear, three Yea and one Nay, and one cosponsorship, the No Secrets for Data Centers Act of 2026. The data does not include bill text, committee assignments, or the content of any vote, so it cannot show whether the money and the votes align. It also cannot show causation, and the page's own note says placement in date order is not a claim that one event caused another.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no record of meetings, no lobbying disclosures, no committee membership, and no indication of which of these bills concern data centers, power, or compute specifically. A reader can see that AI-adjacent money reached this member and that he voted on AI-adjacent bills. A reader cannot conclude from this data alone what either meant.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Jamie Raskin: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 18 events.
